title: Why 100K followers didn't save my startup: build a real product and non-social distribution
summary: Dagobert recounts building 100K X followers while his 5-year startup never exceeded $4K/month. Audience helped early (to $3K MRR) but hit diminishing returns at 10K followers, and chasing followers made him neglect fixing the product and building other channels. Success requires a real problem, a great product, and at least one durable distribution channel.

principles.text: A big following is a consequence of success, not its cause; don't assume successful founders got there via followers.
principles.quote: The fact that they have followers is a consequence of sharing their journey towards success, not the reason for their success in the first place.

principles.text: Business success requires three things: a real problem solved, a great product, and at least one distribution channel.
principles.quote: To make it big in business, you need to solve a real problem + build a great product + figure out at least one distribution channel. There is no way around it.

principles.text: Social audience gives strong early gains but diminishing returns past a few thousand to 10K followers.
principles.quote: Building my audience did help us grow from $300 to $3,000 monthly revenue at the beginning.

principles.text: When a channel plateaus and eats your time, step back, fix the product and build other channels instead of chasing vanity followers.
principles.quote: At this point I should’ve taken a step back, focus on fixing my product, and built other distribution channels.

principles.text: Successful founders with big audiences pair solving real problems with long-term acquisition channels like affiliation or SEO.
principles.quote: they build long-term acquisition channels like affiliation or SEO

principles.text: Grow to a few thousand followers early for friends, partnerships, media and initial traffic, then get back into the trenches of building the business.
principles.quote: But once you start to be a little bit established, your time is better spent being in the trenches and doing the hard work of growing a real business.
